ALLPOWERS P1800

$419–$439

Good budget value

My verdict: Yes, but with reservations. The P1800 looks attractive for camping, occasional power outages, and running everyday appliances. However, I would not buy it solely because of its impressive advertised specifications.

The biggest concern is that independent real-world testing and warranty information are less convincing than those of more established competitors.

What's particularly good:

LiFePO4 battery chemistry, generally preferable for long-term cycle life.

1,800 W output can run many household appliances.

Two powerful 140 W USB-C ports.

Fast AC charging, advertised at approximately 80% in one hour.

Relatively compact for its power output.

The drawbacks I'd pay attention to
Important buying considerations

No independent capacity test yet. The advertised 1,024 Wh hasn't been independently verified in the reviews I found.

Warranty confusion. Some listings advertise five years, but the US warranty policy reportedly provides a shorter base warranty and doesn't clearly identify the P1800 as a five-year model.

No expansion capability. You cannot add another battery to increase capacity.

Conflicting specifications. Published cycle life and UPS switching times differ between some listings.

Unclear safety certification. One independent review found no verifiable safety certification for this particular model.

These are meaningful concerns, particularly if you're buying it for emergency home backup.
